title: Boolean functions of fixed mean with no almost-forcing sub-half-size coalition
author: Jean Bourgain, Jeff Kahn, and Gil Kalai
work: Influential Coalitions for Boolean Functions I: Constructions
source_version: Theory of Computing20 (2024), Article4, publisher source publicationSeptember 30, 2024; DOI10.4086/toc.2024.v020a004

source_locator.proof_scope: Includes author core preliminary constructions at listed proof/context pages

source_scope_convention.meaning: Authors explicitly suppress floor/ceiling/integrality symbols; proof establishes asymptotic mean and then shrinks support. No literal arbitrary-real exact finite-cube cardinality claim is added.

difficulty_reason: The selected existence theorem requires constructing one Boolean function that simultaneously defeats every coalition of size at most (1/2−δ)n while keeping an arbitrary prescribed fixed mean. Section3 chooses a random CNF at the logarithmic clause-length scale and combines uniform coalition avoidance with a second-moment estimate for its density; the construction and simultaneous quantitative constraints are substantive obligations beyond ordinary qualification-exam concentration exercises.

source_check.note: The full mathematical article and original bibliography are retained, including the definitions of J_S^+, the random CNF construction, both supporting lemmas and the complete authored proof of Theorem1.1. Its source-local core lies in Section3; KKL and standard concentration facts remain accurately cited. Theorem1.2 has the separate exponential influence obstruction and ClaimsA–E, all retained as uncounted context in this prototype.
